title: Sterile allogeneic spongioflex® allografts as partial meniscal replacement after incomplete meniscal loss, an investigator initiated trial
official: Sterile allogeneic spongioflex® allografts as partial meniscal replacement after incomplete meniscal loss, an investigator-initiated trial
summary: Main objective: The objective is to improve the meniscus functionality. The efficacy of the procedure will be evalated using the PROMS (IKDC, KOOS, VAS-pain-score). The comparison of the PROMs between patients operated and not operated will be performed and a comparison between PROMs at the beginning of the study and after 2 and 5 years. The clinical trial will be conducted in compliance with the protocol, the CTR 536/2014 and with this Regulation and with the principles of good clinical practice.
conditions: Derangement of posterior horn of medial meniscus
Derangement of anterior horn of medial meniscus
Bucket handle tear of medial meniscus of knee
Bucket handle tear of lateral meniscus
Old bucket handle tear of medial meniscus
Other and unspecified derangement of medial meniscus
Derangement of posterior horn of lateral meniscus
Derangement of meniscus not elsewhere classified
Derangement of anterior horn of lateral meniscus
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Partial loss of portions of the lateral meniscus and lateral joint line pain OR - Partial loss of the medial meniscus and medial joint line pain
2. Age 18-60 years
3. written consent to the study and to provide the scientific data in pseudonymized form
4. sufficient standing of the peripheral rim, so that the procedure can be performed
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of anterior cruciate ligament insufficiency that is not resolved by reconstruction of the anterior cruciate ligament within 16 weeks after partial meniscal implantation.
2. Chronic pain patients
3. inflammatory arthritis or synovitis on the treated knee
4. only for patients who will be operated: -       with increased anesthesiological risk, e.g. with known or predicted difficult airway  -       with increased risk of bleeding  -       with increased risk of infection -       with necrotic, infected or poorly perfused host sides  -       history of allergic reactions or acute hypersensitivity reactions to the IMP or any of its excipients  -      pregnant woman
5. Axial deviation (>2° varus or valgus)
6. realignment osteotomy not performed within 12 weeks
7. advanced cartilage damage (grade III according to ICRS) and osteoarthrosis in the affected compartment (grade III according to Kellgren and Lawrence (Kellgren and Lawrence, 1957)
8. Extension deficit of more than 3° compared to the opposite side or a knee flexion of less than 125°
9. BMI greater than 30 kg/m²
10. <18 years, >60 years
11. pregnancy (only for patients with surgery)
